thread:
maya: Heads-up — I opened a docs PR for the OptKit prefetch + quant guidance (PR #3487). There's a failing lint in the Go SDK snippet and a mismatch between the Python example and the quant profile table. Can someone eyeball?

devon: on it. which snippet is failing lint? the prefetch example or the batch config?

maya: the Go prefetch example. CI shows `gofmt` and `golint` failures, but the code still compiles. Also noticed the Python sample uses `quant_profile='q4_0'` while the table recommends q4_1 for short-sequence conversational workloads.

priya: pinging from Docs QA — is the intent to recommend q4_1 in examples, or only in the table? we should keep examples consistent with the recommended profile for latency-sensitive chat.

alex: I think examples should reflect the recommended default. If q4_1 is the preferred default for short sequences, update both the Python snippet and the table. Also small nit: the Go snippet uses a deprecated helper `MakePrefetcher()` — we moved to `prefetch.NewClient()` last month.

maya: good catch. I'll update the table and the Go snippet. devon, can you share the minimal fix for the Go lint so I can push to the PR?

devon: here's the diff I tested locally — fixes imports and error checks. you can paste into the PR:```go
import (
    "context"
    "log"

    "github.com/redwood/inference-sdk/prefetch"
)

func example() {
    ctx := context.Background()
    client := prefetch.NewClient()
    defer client.Close()

    resp, err := client.Prefetch(ctx, "model-name", prefetch.Options{Batching: true})
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("prefetch failed: %v", err)
    }
    _ = resp
}
```

maya: perfect. I'll paste that in. priya, do you want me to also add a short note in the table row about "short seq chat" use-case?

priya: yes please — something like: "For short conversational turns, prefer q4_1 for better accuracy at similar latency; for very large context / cost-sensitive workloads consider q4_0." Keep it one line.

maya: done — updated the table row and changed the Python snippet to set quant_profile="q4_1". Pushed a commit to the PR (force-push to clean up history).

ci-bot: CI status: docs-lint — failed on staging linkcheck (1 broken link)

maya: ugh, linkcheck broke — which link?

ci-bot: LinkCheck: /optimize/heuristics -> 404 (in file docs/optkit/guide.md line 112)

alex: that's the internal heuristics anchor; I moved it during the restructure. Should be /optimize/heuristics#batching-recommendations. I'll update the link in the PR.

maya: updated. also added a short inline comment explaining why q4_1 is preferred for short seqs.

devon: quick thought — we should add a one-line SDK note about when to prefer KV prefetch vs prefix caching; people often confuse them. maybe a tiny sidenote under the prefetch snippet.

priya: agree — add a bolded one-liner: "Use KV prefetch when repeated key lookups dominate; use prefix caching for repeated prefix completions."

maya: added that note and a small cross-link to the caching playground. Pushed again.

ci-bot: CI status: docs-lint — all checks passed (staging).

alex: looks good to me. approving the PR now. :thumbsup:

priya: LGTM from QA.

maya: thanks all. I'll merge after the 10-min wait to let netlify do its deploy. If anything else pops up I'll open a follow-up thread.

devon: thanks — can we also add a quick test snippet in the SDK CI that runs the examples folder through `gofmt` and the Python samples through `black` to avoid regressions? small follow-up issue would be ideal.

maya: filing an issue now: https://github.com/redwood/inference-docs/issues/429 — "Enforce formatting on examples" — feel free to add notes.

alex: added a comment to the issue suggesting a pre-commit hook on examples/ and a lightweight GH action for formatting.

maya: merged - PR #3487 merged to main. thanks everyone! :tada:

priya: nice! can we add the merged note to the weekly docs sync agenda so other teams know the default changed to q4_1?

maya: yep — adding to this week's agenda.
